new.st: The 1858 Geil & Jones map of Branch County letters 'Branch County Agricultural Grounds' north of Coldwater village, on the east side of the road running NNW from Grand Street. The label is placed on the map; no outline of the grounds is drawn. Pin measured from the inset against the USGS Coldwater West 1960 street grid.
new.t: Today's use not yet checked; much of this edge of Coldwater has since been built up. If it is built over, look-only. Otherwise ask the landowner. Gathering grounds: under the oldest trees, the flat where the crowd stood, the track edges and where wagons parked.
src: Geil & Jones, Map of Branch County, Michigan (1858), Coldwater inset (Library of Congress 2012593022)
pinev: Label spot on the 1858 inset (no outline drawn), measured against the 1960 USGS street grid; about 250 m
new.tovw: Lead grade C (early Michigan fairgrounds thread)

new.pl: North of Grand River St, east of the village, near Mizner's Washington Heights Addition (E1/2 SE1/4 sec. 36); FAIR AVE on the 1895 atlas
new.v: Fairground coin and token drops from 19th-century county fairs
new.st: The 1880 county history puts the fair grounds north of Grand River Street, east of the village, near Mizner's Washington Heights Addition. In August 1875 Mizner offered to trade 'the present grounds for more land further east'. The 1895 Standard Atlas draws no fair ground but keeps a Fair Avenue on the addition's west side, and the 1907 USGS map draws nothing, so the grounds were gone by then. The pin sits on the block just east of Fair Ave and covers both phases.
new.t: Lost fairground: only Fair Ave remains. Probably built over: look-only if so. Gathering grounds: under the oldest trees, the flat where the crowd stood, the track edges and where wagons parked.
src: Standard Atlas of Livingston County (1895) (Library of Congress 2007633239)
pinev: Block east of Fair Ave on the 1895 atlas, north of Grand River Ave; covers the pre- and post-1875 grounds; about 250 m
